segments: to necromancers,
and they prophesied to her
that she would rule and attach herself to whomsoever she wished.
And because of this, she plotted to kill the boy, her son.
And when her secret scheme was revealed,
the nobles expelled and banished her, along with the sorceresses, her companions,
to whom the prophetic word says:
"Stand up now with your enchantments and with your sorceries,
perhaps you can profit;
you are wearied in the multitude of your counsels."
(Isaiah 47:
And in this same year, heavy rains fell,
and swept away large stones and hills.
And even a portion of the mountain broke off
and fell into the torrent of Bet Abdahar, a fortress near the village of Tarshanna.
And the flow of the Euphrates was blocked for about three hours,
and the water reached as far as the village of Prosidin,
which is situated at the top of the mountain.
And then the dam burst (or: the barriers were breached) at the foot of the mountain of Claudias,
and the waters flowed forth,
and wrought great destruction in Syria.
And in this year, pestilence raged among the people of Damietta,
and about twelve thousand souls died,
and many courtyards were emptied of their inhabitants.
And when Nur al-Din marched again against Damascus,
the Franks assembled to the aid of the Damascenes.
And when Nur al-Din heard [this],
he returned to Aleppo.
And in this year, which is the year 546
— 540 {OCR: 546?} of the Arabs —
Saladin went out from the presence of Najm al-Din Ayyub, his father,
who was the governor of Baalbek,
and came to Aleppo to {OCR: ܨܝܕ for ܝܝܕ} his uncle Asad al-Din Shirkuh.
And he brought him in before Nur al-Din,
and he received him
and gave him stipends.
And in the year 1464
— 1464 of the Greeks —
which is the year 547
— 547 of the Arabs —
(1153 of our Lord):
the King of Jerusalem quarreled with {OCR: ܥܡ for ܫܲܡ} his mother,
and the Queen fortified herself in the Tower of David.
Then the nobles mediated between them,
and it was agreed that Jerusalem should belong to the Queen,
and the rest of the cities and the armies to the King, her son.
And that King went against the city of Ascalon,
which was in the hands of the Egyptian Arabs,
and he erected against it a wooden tower and mangonels,
and made a breach in it.
And when four hundred Templar {Fratres} brothers leaped and entered inside the breach,
the Arabs killed all of them,
because twenty thousand armed men were standing inside the breach.
